title: Layers Upon Layers
statementMd:
A peculiar chef is making a cake with several layers, with each layer having a flavor. He has already baked n layers, each with a flavor fi.

However, the chef believes the cake tastes best if the layers are arranged in a specific way: for each pair of adjacent layers, the last letter of the lower layer's flavor must be the same as the first letter of the flavor of the layer directly above it.

For example, listing the layers from the bottom up, the order `apple`, `eggnog`, `gingerbread` is valid. The order `apple`, `dominos` is not valid, since `e` is not the same as `d`. The order `apple`, `extra`, `apple` is valid.

In addition to arranging his layers, he can also do the following to **at most** one layer:

- Flip the layer, which reverses the flavor's name. So, a layer with the flavor `apple` flipped would have the flavor `elppa`.

The chef wishes to use all n of his layers exactly once. Given f1,f2,…,fn, find if he is able to make a valid arrangement for his cake.

## Input

The first line will contain n (1≤n≤105), the number of layers the baker has.

Each of the next n lines contains a string fi (1≤|fi|≤12), the flavor of the i-th layer, consisting only of lowercase Latin letters.

## Output

If the chef cannot build a valid cake, print `NO`.

Otherwise, print `YES` followed by an integer x. Print x=−1 to flip no layer, or print the index x (1≤x≤n) of the layer to flip.

If there are multiple valid answers, print any of them. Any x is accepted as long as the chef can build a valid cake by flipping layer x (or by flipping nothing, if x=−1).

## Note

In the first example, no layer needs to be flipped: `apple` ends in `e` and `eggnog` starts with `e`, and `eggnog` ends in `g` and `gingerbread` starts with `g`.

In the second example, flipping layer 2 turns `cb` into `bc`. Then `ab`, `bc`, `cd` is a valid cake. Without flipping, no valid cake exists.

In the third example, `cake` ends in `e` and `dough` ends in `h`, but the two flavors start with `c` and `d`. No arrangement works, even if either layer is flipped.
